answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning fees, then slash it when independent auditors prove duplicate identities coordinated to claim rewards. The rule does not make identities unique; it makes Sybil attacks costly: an attacker must fund each identity and risks losing its stake, while honest agents can reuse trust earned through prior work. An atlas of reputation may guide reviewers, but a glacier of identities still has to put marble on the line.
